Package io.webagent4j.recording

Class JsonWorkflowRecordingV2Codec

java.lang.Object
io.webagent4j.recording.JsonWorkflowRecordingV2Codec
All Implemented Interfaces:
IWorkflowRecordingV2Codec
public final class JsonWorkflowRecordingV2Codec extends Object implements IWorkflowRecordingV2Codec
Canonical JSON IWorkflowRecordingV2Codec.

This is the Recording V2 counterpart of JsonWorkflowRecordingCodec, following the identical encoding/decoding discipline that class documents in full - canonical fixed field order, always-emit-optional-as-null, streaming JsonGenerator rather than annotation-driven POJO mapping, strict decoding that rejects duplicate keys/unknown fields/wrong JSON types/unsupported schema versions/invalid enums without ever echoing external data back into a thrown message, and deterministic resource bounds enforced before the allocation each one protects. That discipline is not repeated in full here; only what is new for V2's tree-plus-plan shape is documented below. The low-level decode helpers (field lookup, type checks, enum resolution, and so on) are a deliberate separate copy of JsonWorkflowRecordingCodec's own - see RecordedWorkflowStepV2's Javadoc for the same "no compile-time dependency on V1" rationale.

Two independently bounded tree shapes, each with its own node-count and nesting-depth limit: a recording carries both a WorkflowExecutionPlan (every structurally possible branch, both THEN and ELSE/NONE) and a RecordedExecutionNodeV2 tree (only the branch each conditional actually selected). These are separate recursive JSON structures with separate MAX_PLAN_NODES/MAX_NODES counters, each incremented and checked before the node it counts is allocated - so a hostile plan cannot exhaust the node budget meant for the execution tree, or vice versa. Nesting depth for both is bounded by RecordingV2PlanTreeValidator.MAX_TREE_DEPTH - this module's single source of truth for that bound, also enforced by WorkflowRecordingV2's own compact constructor, so this decoder defines no independent copy of the value. Depth is checked explicitly by this decoder's own recursive descent - independent of, and strictly tighter than, the JSON parser's own StreamReadConstraints nesting limit - because this decoder's node-by-node reconstruction recurses in step with the JSON structure: bounding only the parser's tree-building recursion would leave this decoder's own recursive methods still exposed to a StackOverflowError from a document deep enough to pass the parser but not this stricter check. The encode side enforces the identical bound before ever descending into a node's children or branches, so decode(encode(recording)) never fails for depth reasons that encode itself could have refused up front.
